title: Seikilos epitaph: the ancient Greece song that survived millennia
hook: Discover the secret story behind the ancient Greece song of Seikilos, the world's oldest complete melody.

beats.say: Imagine a melody echoing from 2nd-century BC Delphi, sung by a blind lyre-player named Seikilos.
beats.visual: marble column with Seikilos epitaph Delphi

beats.say: His epitaph, carved on a marble column, is the oldest complete musical notation discovered.
beats.visual: ancient Greek marble column inscription close up

beats.say: The notes read A-E-A-G-F-E, a simple Phrygian mode that sounds hauntingly familiar today.
beats.visual: musical notation A E A G F E ancient Greek

beats.say: Scholars once thought the tune was a hymn to Dionysus, but context shows it was a love lament.
Archaeologists dated the stone to around 200 BC, aligning with the Hellenistic era's flourishing of personal poetry.
The melody's rhythm matches the iambic dimeter of contemporary epigrams, linking music to everyday speech.
When a modern musician reconstructed it, the haunting refrain sparked viral TikTok covers, reviving ancient sound.
Yet the original performance likely occurred in a modest temple courtyard, not a grand theater.
Its survival owes a lucky stone slab, spared by a fire that destroyed nearby shrines.
Now you can hear the ancient Greece song of Seikilos, a bridge across two millennia of silence.
